async/lock#

Cancellation-safe cooperative mutual exclusion.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let lock is Lock = Lock();

async update() {
    let guard is LockGuard = await lock.guard();
    defer guard.close();

    await repository.replace(next_value);
}

Description#

Cancellation-safe cooperative mutual exclusion.

Synopsis.

guard() suspends until it owns the lock and returns the ownership capability. The guard has no public constructor: only a successful acquisition can produce one. It is a resource: its owner releases the lock when it goes (scope exit, early return, unwinding), and close() releases it earlier (#846).

Acquirers are granted ownership in FIFO order. Cancelling a waiting guard() future removes that request without consuming the next ownership grant. LockGuard.close() is idempotent.

locked() is an observation for diagnostics and tests, not a safe precondition for another operation: ownership may change immediately after it returns. A lock is not reentrant; attempting to acquire it again while retaining its guard waits like any other acquisition.

Prefer a task which owns mutable state and receives commands through a channel when that shape expresses the domain. Use Lock for genuinely shared resource boundaries which cannot naturally have one state-owning task.
